Claire Reynolds

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 11, Travis County, Texas · Challenger

Attorney. She prosecuted attorney misconduct in the State Bar of Texas attorney discipline department and is a former journalist.

Claire Reynolds is an Austin attorney and the Democratic nominee for Texas' 11th Congressional District. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary over Pedro Ruiz with 57.4% of the vote. In the November 3, 2026 general election she faces incumbent Republican August Pfluger.

Where Reynolds stands

Minimum wage
Supports a federal $17/hour minimum wage indexed to inflation. She says she would personally raise it to $25/hour.
Immigration and border
Supports demilitarizing the southern border and fully funding asylum review and guest-worker programs. Supports defunding and abolishing ICE.
Policing
Supports ending qualified immunity and setting federal police accountability standards.
Higher education
Supports federal student debt cancellation and tuition-free public college.
Campaign finance
Supports banning corporate PAC money and creating public financing for campaigns.
Data centers and electricity rates
Said Senate Democrats should not have blocked the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340), which would make large data centers pay for grid upgrades. She called the bill weak but 'still a good start.'
Executive power
Opposes the president taking ownership stakes in private companies. Says Congress should pass a law taking that authority back.

Background

  • Born in Indiana; raised in central Illinois
  • B.S. in journalism, Northwestern University (Medill School)
  • J.D., University of San Diego School of Law; passed the California bar
  • Former journalist
  • Moved to Texas in 2007; lives in Austin
  • Attorney in the State Bar of Texas attorney discipline department (more than 10 years)
  • Won the 2026 Democratic primary for TX-11 (57.4%)
